readme:
# Orca 迭代级动态批处理

## 1. 问题

让请求按到达顺序进入每轮空闲槽，完成即退出批次。

已完成prefill的离散生成迭代模拟，固定每轮一时间单位、每个活跃请求生成一token；不模拟selective batching算子。

原文: [Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models](https://www.usenix.org/conference/osdi22/presentation/yu) · Section 3, S1 and Figure 4: iteration-level scheduling; Section 4.2, Algorithm 1: FCFS admission.

## 2. 核心公式

$$
C_i=1+\max\{t:i\in B_t\},\qquad |B_t|\le K,\qquad \sum_t\mathbf{1}[i\in B_t]=L_i.
$$

## 3. 公式到代码

- `iteration_schedule(arrivals: list[int], lengths: list[int], capacity: int) -> tuple[list[tuple], list[int]]` — Per-iteration active request IDs and completion times in original order.

为每个请求维护剩余token。执行前接纳已到达且未开始的请求，执行后减少剩余量并立即释放完成请求。不能等整批最慢请求结束后才接纳新请求。

## 4. 本题约定

arrivals 与 lengths 为等长 Python 整数列表；到达>=0，长度>=1，capacity>=1。相同时刻按输入索引排序。每轮开头按 (arrival,index) 补满空位，已有请求不被抢占；完成时间为最后执行时隙右端。返回 (batches, completion_times)，空闲时隙保留空tuple。

## 5. 交互图

回放 6 个同时到达的异长请求，与请求级固定批次对照完成时间；扫描容量 1、2、3，比较平均延迟和占用槽。

T3 使用实际待测函数生成实验，网页参考图使用参考实现。数值来自教学样本，不表示GPU吞吐或完整模型质量。

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 延伸

结合所引章节，解释本题保留了哪些维度、状态或调度约束，再扩展实验样本并保持已有契约。更大模型、真实设备与通信代价需要单独测量。

en.readme:
# Orca Iteration-Level Dynamic Batching

## 1. Problem

Admit requests into free slots each iteration and release them immediately on completion.

Discrete generation replay after prefill, with unit-duration iterations and one token per active request; selective-batching operators are outside this kernel.

Source: [Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models](https://www.usenix.org/conference/osdi22/presentation/yu) · Section 3, S1 and Figure 4: iteration-level scheduling; Section 4.2, Algorithm 1: FCFS admission.

## 2. Core equations

$$
C_i=1+\max\{t:i\in B_t\},\qquad |B_t|\le K,\qquad \sum_t\mathbf{1}[i\in B_t]=L_i.
$$

## 3. From equations to code

- `iteration_schedule(arrivals: list[int], lengths: list[int], capacity: int) -> tuple[list[tuple], list[int]]` — Per-iteration active request IDs and completion times in original order.

Track remaining tokens. Admit ready pending requests before executing, decrement active requests afterward, and immediately release completed slots. Admission does not wait for the slowest member of the old batch.

## 4. Conventions

arrivals and lengths are equal-length integer lists; arrivals>=0, lengths>=1, capacity>=1. Break arrival ties by input index. Fill slots at each iteration boundary in (arrival,index) order without preempting active requests. Completion is the end of the final occupied slot. Return (batches, completion_times), preserving idle slots as empty tuples.

## 5. Experiment view

Replay six simultaneous requests of unequal length, compare completions with request-level fixed batches, and sweep capacities 1, 2 and 3 for latency and slot occupancy.

The chart is generated by the actual submitted kernel during T3 and by the reference during export. Values are synthetic teaching measurements, not GPU throughput or full-model quality claims.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Further study

Read the cited section and explain which dimensions or scheduling constraints the kernel preserves. Then extend the experiment beyond the stated fixture while retaining the existing contract. Larger models, real devices, and communication costs require separate measurement.

# Orca Iteration-Level Dynamic Batching — Solution notes

## Derivation and implementation

Track remaining tokens. Admit ready pending requests before executing, decrement active requests afterward, and immediately release completed slots. Admission does not wait for the slowest member of the old batch.

$$
C_i=1+\max\{t:i\in B_t\},\qquad |B_t|\le K,\qquad \sum_t\mathbf{1}[i\in B_t]=L_i.
$$

## Boundary and gradient ownership

arrivals and lengths are equal-length integer lists; arrivals>=0, lengths>=1, capacity>=1. Break arrival ties by input index. Fill slots at each iteration boundary in (arrival,index) order without preempting active requests. Completion is the end of the final occupied slot. Return (batches, completion_times), preserving idle slots as empty tuples.

## Independent checks

T0 checks the callable contract and invalid boundaries. T1 uses hand calculations or an independent scalar formulation. T2 checks invariances, state conservation, gradients when meaningful, or atomic state changes. T3 invokes the supplied implementation in the deterministic experiment; it does not compare two imports of the same reference.

## Behavioral experiment

Replay six simultaneous requests of unequal length, compare completions with request-level fixed batches, and sweep capacities 1, 2 and 3 for latency and slot occupancy.

Discrete generation replay after prefill, with unit-duration iterations and one token per active request; selective-batching operators are outside this kernel.

### Reference calibration

Deterministic CPU fixture; Python 3.14.2, PyTorch 2.14.1.

| Metric | Reference value |
| --- | ---: |
| dynamic_mean_latency | 3.5 |
| static_mean_latency | 7 |
| tokens_executed | 11 |

## Common mistakes

- m1_batch_barrier: Holding admission until an old batch drains wastes released slots.
- m2_completion_start: Completion occurs at the end, not the start, of an iteration.
